meta.scope: Morphology module for lemmatization (orthography, particles, pronouns, possessives, determiners, derivation, reduplication, register). Syntax and Semantics of GOLD not populated.

pronouns.possessive_note: dual/plural pronominal element: plural = dual + -u (S1 ch.20 par.14)

rules.input_pattern: glottal stop written ʻ (U+02BB) in the dictionary; inverted apostrophe (‘) in the grammar; may be absent in some headwords
rules.operation: for matching: delete all of [ʻ ‘ ’ ' ʼ `] from both the form and the lexicon key; keep the dictionary spelling (U+02BB) as output
rules.notes: Grammar states the inverted apostrophe represents the glottal stop wherever it occurs (Privy Council 1943). Dictionary headwords use U+02BB (86 occurrences) but some headwords omit it (alu, oku) where the grammar writes ʻalu, ʻoku. Other encodings (straight, right-quote, U+02BC) are not described in the sources: treated only as normalization targets (see gaps).

rules.input_pattern: long vowels ā ē ī ō ū (macron)
rules.operation: for matching: remove macron; recover lemma from lexicon key; two headwords may differ only by the macron
rules.notes: Grammar: normal vs long vowel often distinguishes meaning (e.g. kaka/kāka/kākā, mo/mō). Dictionary writes macrons (ā 60, ō 13, ē 13, ī 6, ū 1).

rules.input_pattern: acute accent for stress (final-vowel stress, definitive accent): falé, ngāué, ʻalú
rules.operation: delete U+0301 and any acute on a final vowel; lemma = unaccented form
rules.notes: Grammar recommends marking only stressed final vowels other than macron vowels; the definitive accent shifts to the end of the nounal group. The dictionary does not mark stress.

rules.input_pattern: word division: preposition, article and pronoun written apart; tense sign apart from pronoun; conjunction apart from pronoun; pé and taʻe, kei, mei apart; fie apart
rules.operation: tokenize at spaces; do not merge. Compounds written as one word keep one lemma

examples.gloss: compound of tama + siʻi (as written in grammar)

rules.notes: Written-as-one compounds named in grammar: tamaiki, meʻakai, vakapuna, manupuna, mamani (vs mama ni), faʻahitaʻu, tangataʻeiki; all possessive pronouns and pronominal adjectives are written as one word.

rules.input_pattern: capitalised proper names; pos "name" in dictionary
rules.operation: lemma = capitalised name as headword (incl. ʻ and macron)

rules.input_pattern: obsolete spelling variants: b for p, j for s (and other differences)
rules.operation: lemma = alt_of target given in the dictionary (lexicon lookup); b→p and j→s are described in the grammar as replaced by p and s

rules.notes: Dictionary has 16 alt-of pairs (14 tagged obsolete, 2 alternative). Classes among the 16 pairs: macron/ʻ differences only 5 (Me/Mē, Sepitema/Sēpitema, Epeleli/ʻEpeleli, Aokosi/ʻAokosi, Novema/Nōvema); b→p 3 (behe, Bilitania, Okatoba); j→s 3 (June, Julai, Januali); other 5. No class has ≥10 forms, so no default_replacement is recorded.

rules.input_pattern: ʻoku | kuo | naʻa | naʻe | ne | te | ʻe | he | ka (tense signs)
rules.operation: keep as separate token; provisional lemma = the sign itself (dictionary headwords: te, ne, naʻe particles; oku verb "to be")

rules.notes: Dictionary has no entries for kuo, naʻa, ʻe, he, ka; no source states a lemma for tense signs, so the choice (sign itself vs normalised naʻa→naʻe, he/ʻe→te) is open. Dictionary lists ʻoku as a verb "to be" (headword oku).

rules.input_pattern: no tense sign after mo, and, ʻo, and; past sign often dropped after pea
rules.operation: no lemma operation; tense is unmarked

rules.input_pattern: preposed cardinal pronouns (subject, enclitic) and postposed forms (table above)
rules.operation: provisional: the dictionary lemmatizes the 1sg to the postposed form au (ou alt-of au) but 3sg to preposed ne; no other pronoun has an entry. Per-person lemma candidates are in pronouns.cardinal
rules.notes: Five 1sg exclusive forms (au, ou, ku, u, kau): ou after ʻoku; ku after naʻa; u after kuo, ne, te, ka, ke, pea, mo, ʻo; kau sentence-initially. Choice of lemma (preposed vs postposed) is not fixed by any source.

rules.input_pattern: ne (preposed 3sg), ia, kinaua, nau, kinautolu; ia/ne sometimes refer to inanimates
rules.operation: lemma candidates in table; ne also = past sign, ia also = demonstrative

examples.gloss: he, she, it, occasionally they in reference to inanimate objects
examples.translation: he, she, it, occasionally they in reference to inanimate objects

rules.input_pattern: kita "one"; also in siokita, taʻesiokita, fakaekita
rules.operation: lemma kita (indefinite one, or humble I/me)

examples.translation: one (indefinite), or I/me in polite speech

rules.input_pattern: possessive pronouns: 12 possessors x (definite, indefinite) x (ordinary, emotional) + emphatic, in two ranks (a-class "subjective", o-class "objective")
rules.operation: provisional lemma = the form itself (dictionary headword hoku "my"; dual/plural = singular + -u pattern in grammar); alternative analysis = article + ʻa/ʻo + cardinal pronoun (he ʻa ku → heʻeku)
rules.notes: Full table in pronouns.possessive_forms. 73 words per rank (1 preposition ʻa/ʻo, 60 possessive pronouns, 12 pronominal adjectives); 146 in all (ch.13 par.6-8). The grammar states that dual/plural forms add -u to the dual in the structure tables and that heʻe- forms (not ʻe-) appear after ʻe, ʻi, ki, mei; the second person has no elided form. Emotional forms: in the objective rank siʻ- replaces h-; 13 of the 24 emotional forms are identical in the two ranks (ch.20 par.17).

rules.input_pattern: a-class vs o-class selection (ʻeku vs hoku)
rules.operation: select by meaning of relation, not by form: a-class (subjective: possessor active, influential towards the thing: goods, tools, animals owned, food, persons in one's employ; also the possessor corresponding to the subject of a verbal noun); o-class (objective: thing constitutes/represents/affects the possessor: body, mind, parts, clothing, relatives, friends, things provided; possessor corresponding to the object of a verbal noun)
rules.notes: Class depends on the head noun (lexicon-dependent); listed exceptions: toki, huo, kupenga, tao, pa take the o-class despite being tools (ch.13 par.22); ʻinu, ʻoho, kofi, koko take it for food/drink (par.25).

rules.input_pattern: hano/hono "anticipative" before a noun followed by ʻo; hono kotoa "its whole"
rules.operation: lemma = hono/hano (no base noun recovery)

rules.input_pattern: pronominal adjectives ʻaʻaku/ʻaku, ʻoʻoku/ʻoku, ʻamaua, ʻomaua, … (preposition ʻa/ʻo + pronoun)
rules.operation: provisional lemma = form; analysis = ʻa/ʻo + pronoun without ki-; ʻoʻoku may be pronounced oku
rules.notes: Homograph risk: ʻoku (pronominal adjective, "oku" pronunciation) vs ʻoku (present tense sign).

rules.input_pattern: pronominal adverbs maʻaku, moʻoku, … (maʻa-/moʻo- + pronoun element) and ai, ʻaki
rules.operation: maʻa-/moʻo- replace ʻa-/ʻo- of the pronominal adjective; provisional lemma = form

rules.input_pattern: he | e (definite), ha (indefinite), siʻi (emotional definite), siʻa (emotional indefinite)
rules.operation: he after ʻe, ʻi, ki, mei; e elsewhere; enclitic after maʻa and moʻo. Dictionary has only ha (indefinite article); no article entry for e/he (dictionary has prep e "by")
rules.notes: Lemma of he/e not fixed: grammar groups them as "he or e"; he also = conj "for, because" (ch.8 par.29-31, light-word list).

rules.input_pattern: demonstratives: ē, hē, pehē (deictic); ni, eni, heni, peheni (near speaker); na, ena, hena, pehena (near hearer); ia (third)
rules.operation: provisional lemma = form; ni/na are enclitic adjectives; heni/hena = ʻi + eni/ena when ʻi is omitted
rules.notes: ni also = "now" (adverb); na also = pronoun "they two"; eni also = "now".

rules.input_pattern: number signs: ongo (dual), kau, fanga, ʻū, ngaahi (plural), tukui, tuʻu, hala (special)
rules.operation: lemma = the sign; do not treat as part of the noun
rules.notes: kau also = 1sg pronoun and = prefix; ʻū = ʻ + ū (sign for things).

rules.input_pattern: prepositions ʻe, ʻa, ko, ki, ʻi, ʻo, mo, maʻa, moʻo, mei, ʻaki, faka, faʻa (grammar ch.3, 16)
rules.operation: lemma = form; ʻe marks the actor, ʻa the thing acted on, ko identity (relation names in grammar, no case terminology)
rules.source: S1 ch.3 par.3-6, ch.16 index; S2
rules.notes: Case values not stated in source; Case=Erg for ʻe and Case=Abs for ʻa would be a task-convention mapping, not source terminology. ʻe also future sign, vocative sign and conj; ʻa also "of"; ko also demonstrative component.

rules.input_pattern: cardinals: noa, taha, ua, tolu, fā, nima, ono, fitu, valu, hiva, hongofulu, uofulu, tolungofulu … , teau, afe; compounds hongofulu mā taha …
rules.operation: lemma = surface form; compound numerals are multiword headwords in the dictionary (hongofulu mā taha = 11)

examples.form: ha kau talavou ʻe toko nima
examples.gloss: a PL young-man PART person five

rules.notes: Dictionary: 40 num entries; 18 are multiword. taha "one" / ua "two" may also act as adjective.

rules.input_pattern: directionals mai, atu, ange, ai, hake, hifo (adverbs); as verbs written ʻatu, ʻange, ʻai
rules.operation: lemma = adverb form; verb use shows initial glottal stop

rules.input_pattern: -ʻi (also -fi, -hi, -i, -ki, -mi, -ni, -ngi, -si): transitive/executive suffixes
rules.operation: strip the suffix; the variant is lexically determined; base must be checked in the lexicon (vowel/reduplication may change: ʻanuhi ← ʻaʻanu)
rules.notes: Dictionary has no verb derived by -ʻi where the base is also a headword (0 attested pairs), so no counts support a default; lemma = base (alt: derived form as own lemma).

rules.input_pattern: -a, -ina, -hia, -na, -kina (durational/impersonal transitive; also adjectival)
rules.operation: strip suffix; -ina/-hia/-na/-kina may be accompanied by vowel change (ʻofa → ʻofeina); lexicon needed
rules.notes: Grammar: such verbs often occur without subject, equivalent to an English passive; no Voice terminology in source.

rules.input_pattern: -a, -fia, -hia, -ia, -ina, -kina, -mia, -ngia, -sia, -ʻia: adjectives / intransitive verbs
rules.operation: strip suffix and recover base from lexicon; -ʻia: noun/adjective base kept intact
rules.notes: Dictionary: fiekaia adj "hungry", kaia absent. Final a becomes ā before -a only with moʻu-.

rules.input_pattern: -ʻaki: noun → verb "treat/use as"; verb → verb "with/about"; also reciprocal-forming after fe-
rules.operation: strip -ʻaki; for reciprocal see PREF-003
rules.notes: Postposed subject of such verbs takes ʻe, showing it is a suffix (written as one word).

rules.input_pattern: -ʻanga (place/means), -nga (thing), -fanga/-nanga/-tanga (special), -a/-ʻa (2 words)
rules.operation: strip suffix; base verb recovered with lexicon; -nga words: nofoʻanga (place) vs … -nga (thing)
rules.source: S1 ch.30 par.5-13; S2 (puleʻanga, kavenga, fōtunga as headwords)
rules.notes: Dictionary headwords with these endings: puleʻanga "kingdom", kavenga "burden" (etymology kawe-ŋa), fōtunga "face", paʻanga: none has its base as a headword (0 pairs).

rules.input_pattern: possessive -ʻi (mataʻi helé, ngakoʻi puaka) and momoʻi, meʻi, foʻi, mataʻi, tahaʻi
rules.operation: strip -ʻi → noun; ambiguous with transitive -ʻi; foʻi also dictionary verb "to lose"

rules.input_pattern: faka- (likeness; causation; reflexive causative; provide/have), faka-e- (pertaining to), faka-fe-
rules.operation: strip faka-; lemma = base; alternative: derived form as own lemma (record both); reduplicating + faka- (fakapotopoto) see RED-006
rules.notes: Dictionary: 13 faka-initial headword entries (12 distinct); 2 have the remainder as headword (fakaleitī, fakafefine) = 2 of 12. Too few (n<10) for a default. Dictionary also lists faka as preposition "in the manner of" (doublet faʻa).

rules.input_pattern: fe- (reciprocative, reciprocal, communal; alone: fetaki, feʻao, fekai)
rules.operation: strip fe- (and the following suffix -ʻaki/-aki/-i/-ki…); lexicon needed
rules.notes: Irregular: fekeʻikeʻi ← kē, fepaki ← pa?, femoʻuekina ← moʻua. Dictionary has no fe- derived headwords (feke, fekika are unrelated).

rules.input_pattern: ma-, mo-, mā- (potential; resultant state; other)
rules.operation: strip prefix; for reduplicated (mahaehae) see RED-006

examples.gloss: turn over → be able to turn over
examples.translation: to be able to turn over

rules.notes: ma- also = noun/ prefix homograph with ma "bread"/"we two". Dictionary: māfana adj/noun "warm" (from ma-fana) while fana is a verb "to shoot": derived form has its own lemma.

rules.input_pattern: moʻu- + -a (continuation); kaunga- (together, fellow-)
rules.operation: strip prefix (and -a, with final a → ā); lexicon needed

rules.input_pattern: complete reduplication XX (with or without vowel change in the first copy: pekepeka, muʻomuʻa)
rules.operation: if the form is a doubled string, base = second half; accept only if the base is in the lexicon; else keep the form as lemma
rules.notes: Dictionary: 13 headwords have a doubled shape (kisikisi, pēpē, malimali, pepe, anoano, kaukau, huhu, tuitui, vaivai, keke, ʻoneʻone, kumukumu, fanafana); the base is a headword in 3 cases (anoano/ano, ʻoneʻone/ʻone, vaivai/vai?). All have their own entry, so lexicalised reduplications keep their own lemma. n=13 attested forms but base recovered ≤ 3 → no default_replacement.

rules.input_pattern: partial reduplication of the first syllable (lalahi, mamata, fofoʻou, papaʻuli, tutupu, nonofo)
rules.operation: remove the first CV (when it repeats the next CV, allowing vowel change) → base; lexicon needed
rules.notes: Dictionary: kakau "to swim" and loloa "long" are single headwords derived historically from reduplication; kaukau as complete reduplication of kau. These keep their own lemma.

rules.input_pattern: partial reduplication of the later part (havilivili) and middle part (ʻAfifio)
rules.operation: recover base by removing the repeated segment; lexicon needed

rules.input_pattern: reduplication changing meaning: plural/repetition, intensification, moderation, change of part of speech, other
rules.operation: lemma = base unless the reduplicated word has its own dictionary entry
rules.notes: Many reduplicated forms change part of speech (noun→adj/verb) and are lexicalised; dictionary headword vaivai "weak" exists, vai "water" (noun) too.

rules.input_pattern: two reduplication types for the same base (hifihifi vs hihifi, vakuvaku vs vavaku, lomilomi vs lolomi)
rules.operation: pick lemma = base; the two shapes differ in meaning only

rules.input_pattern: faka- + reduplication (fakapotopoto, fakaalaala, fakahangahanga, fakamuʻomuʻa)
rules.operation: remove faka- then undo reduplication; fakamuʻomuʻa is simply causative of muʻomuʻa

examples.gloss: go in front → put in front

rules.input_pattern: special dual/plural forms of nouns, verbs, adjectives (table irregular_forms)
rules.operation: map to the singular by table; lexicon only
rules.notes: OCR of the scan left several table items uncertain (pekia, siʻi/ʻiiki, loloa); only clear items are listed. Dictionary has fafine and fefine as doublets and motuʻa as adj + noun.

rules.input_pattern: five-level lexical equivalents (ordinary, polite, honorific, regal, derogatory), e.g. kai / tokoni / ʻilo / taumafa / mama
rules.operation: each form is its own lemma when it is also an ordinary word (tokoni "help", ʻilo "know", mama "chew"); mapping to the ordinary item is not stated; record as lexicon equivalence
rules.source: S1 ch.36 par.5-8; S2 (lau honorific/polite tag)
rules.notes: Only this one set is attested; the chapter text in the available PDF stops at p.305. Dictionary entry lau "hair" carries tags honorific+polite (no equivalent given); tokoni is a headword "to help".

lexicon_files.citation_form: take `word`; strip the artifact suffix "/languages M to Z"; if senses[].alt_of exists use alt_of[].word; restore ʻ if a variant without ʻ is found in forms[].form
